articles.title: "It'll be certainly emotional": How Tom Brady's return to New England brings back memories of his legendary years with the Patriots
articles.summary: Tom Brady will return to Foxborough on Sunday for the first time as an NFL broadcaster, and the occasion carries more weight than a regular FOX assignment.
articles.body: Tom Brady will return to Foxborough on Sunday for the first time as an NFL broadcaster, and the occasion carries more weight than a regular FOX assignment. The former New England Patriots quarterback will call his old team's Week 9 game against the Green Bay Packers alongside Kevin Burkhardt. The visit also coincides with Rob Gronkowski's induction into the Patriots Hall of Fame. Brady has already admitted that seeing the stadium again will bring back memories of two decades, six Super Bowl titles and some of the biggest moments of his career.Tom Brady opens up about his return to FoxboroughTom Brady spoke about the visit during an appearance on The Herd with Colin Cowherd on Tuesday. He did not hide what the return means to him, explaining that almost every part of Gillette Stadium holds a memory from his playing days."It'll be certainly emotional," Brady admitted to Cowherd. "I mean, every inch of that stadium, I've been through so many times. From the locker rooms to the media rooms to the field. Just so many memorable plays in that stadium. Big games, championship games and rivalry games, division-clinching games. So, to be back there and to really understand what that Patriot organization is all about and to convey that to the fans in a way where I'm not talking about myself, I'm really talking about this awesome program that's been built. And the Patriots just always seem to do things the right way."There is a small but important distinction in Brady's comments. He knows that his name will naturally come up when viewers think about the Patriots' success, but he wants the broadcast to recognise the wider organisation. His return also comes at a time when New England has found fresh momentum under head coach Mike Vrabel.Brady praised Vrabel for changing the team's environment and guiding the Patriots back to the Super Bowl last season. He also credited offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels for helping quarterback Drake Maye develop into an MVP candidate. The comments showed that Brady has followed the franchise's progress even after leaving it.He also welcomed the Packers' visit, calling it a rare meeting between AFC and NFC teams."It's a great AFC-NFC matchup. These don't happen very often," Brady said of Green Bay traveling to New England. "And I get to be there to watch it in person in front of a very friendly home crowd — I'm very excited."Brady's Patriots legacy makes the FOX assignment differentBrady's connection with New England began when the Patriots selected him in the sixth round of the 2000 NFL Draft. He became the starting quarterback a year later after Drew Bledsoe suffered an injury. Few could have predicted what followed.Over 20 seasons, Brady turned the franchise into a championship powerhouse. He won six Super Bowls, reached nine championship games and collected three NFL MVP awards. His partnership with Bill Belichick became one of the most successful player-coach combinations in league history. Brady also threw for 74,571 regular-season yards and 541 touchdowns during his Patriots career.He left New England after the 2019 season, joining Tampa Bay and winning another Super Bowl before retiring after the 2022 campaign. His move to FOX opened a new chapter, but Sunday offers a rare chance to reconnect with the place where most of his greatest achievements happened.FOX also knows the value of this return. Brady reportedly earns upwards of $38 million annually for his broadcasting role, and the network has released a promotional commercial built around his Foxborough visit. It is an unusual level of attention for a broadcaster, but Brady is hardly an ordinary former player.With Gronkowski receiving his Hall of Fame honour and the Patriots hosting Green Bay, the broadcast has plenty of stories beyond the result. Brady will have to cover them without making the afternoon about his own achievements. That may be the hardest part of the assignment for someone whose career is so closely tied to the stadium.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Instead, the pair seem comfortable enjoying their relationship without rushing into marriage.An insider also offered some insight into how they manage their busy personal lives."She likes spending time with him. Between her kids and her career, her plate is very full. articles.title: Justin Rogers faces backlash over Dan Campbell’s press conference as Jack Campbell’s injury sparks an unexpected apology
articles.summary: Detroit Lions reporter Justin Rogers has apologized for asking a football-related question during head coach Dan Campbell’s press conference about
articles.body: Detroit Lions reporter Justin Rogers has apologized for asking a football-related question during head coach Dan Campbell’s press conference about linebacker Jack Campbell’s injury. Rogers admitted that his question could have waited for another day, as the team was still dealing with the shock of the incident. His apology came after the Lions’ 19-15 win over the Minnesota Vikings, which ended with serious concerns about their defensive captain’s health.Justin Rogers apologizes for his question during Dan Campbell’s press conferenceThe situation unfolded on Monday, November 2, when Dan Campbell met with reporters following Detroit’s victory over Minnesota. Much of the press conference focused on Jack Campbell, who had been taken to a local hospital after suffering a frightening injury during Sunday’s game.However, Detroit Football Network reporter Justin Rogers also brought up a football-related question about the Lions’ performance against Minnesota’s aggressive blitz pressure. Dan Campbell answered him, but the question later drew criticism because of the circumstances surrounding the team’s injury concern.Rogers eventually addressed the situation himself on X, accepting that he could have chosen a better time to ask about the game rather than bringing it up during a press conference largely focused on his injured colleague.“Immediately regret working a football/game question into that press conference. Wasn’t the right time and it could have easily waited until Wednesday. Apologies,” Rogers wrote.His message made it clear that he understood why the timing of his question had become an issue. He did not suggest that asking about the game was wrong in itself, but acknowledged that Wednesday’s media availability would have been a more suitable opportunity.According to The Spun, Rogers’ apology also received support from some fans, who felt that he did not need to be so hard on himself for doing his job. Still, his decision to publicly acknowledge the timing showed that he understood the sensitivity of the situation.Jack Campbell’s injury raises concern as Dan Campbell shares an update on his recoveryWhile Rogers’ apology became a talking point, the bigger concern for Detroit remained Jack Campbell’s health. The 26-year-old linebacker was injured early in the fourth quarter against Minnesota, with 14:48 left on the clock.Campbell was involved in a tackle on Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson. During the play, his head appeared to make contact with Hockenson’s hip before he fell face-first onto the field. He remained motionless as medical staff rushed to help him. The Lions eventually placed him on a backboard and took him to a local hospital for further evaluation of a neck injury.Dan Campbell also visited the linebacker at the hospital on Sunday night, where he met his parents and spoke with his wife. Speaking to reporters on Monday, the Lions coach shared a positive account of that visit.“I got to go see him last night. It was good. It was positive. Got to see his parents, talk to his wife. Everybody’s in good spirits. It’s about the recovery, and it’s a small setback. That’s the family. They’re very positive.”The coach also spoke about what Jack means to the team, especially as one of its defensive captains. He made it clear that the linebacker has earned the respect of everyone in the locker room through his character and commitment.“He’s trustworthy. He’s dependable. He’ll give you the shirt off his back. He’s just all heart and all effort. Just an unbelievable person. Down to earth and very genuine. There’s not a man on this team that doesn’t respect Jack Campbell.”The Detroit Lions also released a statement on Monday, confirming that Jack was still receiving care at the hospital. The team said, “Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital. Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family, we will not share further information at this time.”There was another encouraging update on Tuesday, November 3, when Dan Campbell spoke to 97.1 The Ticket. He confirmed that Jack was improving, although the incident remained difficult for everyone around the team.“The good news is he is improving,” the coach said.As reported by ClickOnDetroit, Detroit is now preparing for its Week 9 meeting with the Miami Dolphins on November 8. However, the team has not announced when Jack Campbell could return to the field.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why the 49ers roster construction has been a level above the rest of the NFL
articles.summary: The Niners have regularly had one of the best rosters in the NFL over the past few years.
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers have not been the best drafters in the NFL during the Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch era, at least in recent years. And yet, they've found a way to remain perennial contenders, making a pair of Super Bowls and four NFC Championship Games over a nine-year run, and are currently Super Bowl favorites midway through the 2026 season.

Overall, the 49ers have found a way to compete with top-loaded rosters, while also drafting well in certain years to keep good youth on the team. They've also made requisite trade deadline moves, been aggressive when the situation has called for it, and also benefitted from elite level coaching.

In the NFL, we've seen some teams reach the top, but struggle to return. We've seen others remain in the playoff race year after year, but fail to reach that next level. The 49ers, though, have bounced back through hard years and have made the playoffs in five of the last seven years, with four of those appearances being to the NFC Championship Game and further.

What's been the secret to their success and roster construction? With the trade deadline coming up and another potential chance for the 49ers to improve their roster, I wanted to look at their past history under Lynch and Shanahan to see what separates them from the rest of the NFL.

While many can fault the 49ers for some of their recent draft mistakes this decade, the 49ers built a very strong foundation of stars from their early draft successes.

San Francisco got George Kittle and D.J. Jones in the fifth and sixth rounds of Kyle Shanahan's first draft with the franchise back in 2017. In 2018, they added Fred Warner in the third round. And in 2019, they added Nick Bosa, Deebo Samuel, and Dre Greenlaw to the mix in the first, second, and fifth rounds.

Right there, that's a core of star players that help set the foundation for the 49ers, not only in the early years of the Shanahan era, but all the way to 2026. Kittle, Warner, Bosa, and Samuel ended up earning All-Pro awards. Greenlaw was a regular starter since his rookie year, forming one of the best linebacker tandems in the NFL.

You follow up the strong drafting with quality trades from John Lynch for Jimmy Garoppolo and Trent Williams and even Emmanuel Sanders, and that's what led to the 49ers' first two NFC Championship Game appearances in 2019 and 2021.

It's rare that teams see that level of success, especially outside the first round, in the draft. Now, the 49ers weren't close to perfect. They took Solomon Thomas and Reuben Foster in the first round in 2017, while Akhello Witherspoon, C.J. Beathard, and Joe Williams were their next three picks in the draft. In 2018, they took Dante Pettis in the second round and Tarvarius Moore in the third round. In 2019, they took Jalen Hurd in the third round and Mitch Wishnowsky in the fourth.

There were a fair share of poor evals or draft misses, but the 49ers started their rebuild with a good foundation through the draft that set them straight going forward.

Perhaps the biggest factor that sets the 49ers apart from other teams in the NFL is their contract strategy.

The 49ers have dished out a ton of contracts near or at the top of position markets, like ones to Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, Arik Armstead, Charvarius Ward, and Fred Warner. They've been willing to pay up for their star talents, and those contracts have aged quite well for them, for the most part.

Their mid-level extensions have also panned out well for the most part. Colton McKivitz's three-year, $45 million deal is looking great already. When the 49ers initially signed Dre Greenlaw to a two-year deal worth under $10 million annually a few years back, that was a huge win.

The biggest key is that the 49ers haven't really been hurt as much by the contracts they've handed out. There have been a few poor contracts, such as Dee Ford and Brandon Aiyuk, but the 49ers have gotten out of those deals early. You could even loop Deebo Samuel, Javon Hargrave, or Jimmy Garoppolo's contract into the mix as ones that were beneficial for the 49ers early on, but were ones they moved on from when they needed to.

And the hits have been really good hits. Each of their extensions mentioned above has paid off. And their free-agent splashes have done really well as well. The Niners were early with Charvarius Ward and got high-level play out of him. Same with Richard Sherman a few years back. And this year, Mike Evans is looking like a huge hit.

This has been where other teams have really struggled, be it to move off prior contracts or handing out bad ones in the first place. Nearly every team in the NFL has at least one of those on the books. The 49ers, on the other hand, have done a really good job of getting deals done early, while also getting out of them when they need to.

This is another key area that has separated the 49ers and led to a ton of their success. San Francisco has always been willing to flip capital for star players. They sent two draft picks for Trent Williams back in 2020. They traded for Christian McCaffrey at the deadline in 2022. They went after Chase Young the year after.

San Francisco has made some major moves, as well as a ton of minor moves to position themselves well. They've also usually looked for multi-year value from their trades, which has worked wonders from a value perspective.

Whether it was a small deadline move for Charles Omenihu or even the recent splash for DeForest Buckner, the 49ers have generally navigated the trade deadline well without overpaying with draft capital. Then, in the offseason, they've also been willing to make moves as well.

These other avenues of improving the roster, be it contract management or trades, help offset when the 49ers whiff on draft picks. And the positives have come much more often than the negatives.

I do think the 49ers have understood and captured positional value as well when handing out contracts. The Niners have generally shied away from paying defensive backs and offensive linemen marquee money, though they're willing to hand out contracts to the right players.

We've seen a ton of defensive back moves and contracts age quite poorly over the past few years, which have really hurt a number of teams aspiring to be contenders. The 49ers have instead prioritized other positions, such as defensive line and wide receiver.

Overall, though, the total number of factors all contribute to why the 49ers have been able to build a sustainable roster construction model that has outlasted a ton of its NFL counterparts. So, even when they're struggling to draft well, the foundation for roster building remains there and can be capitalized on in different ways.

articles.title: Vikings May Be Cooling on Star Running Back Trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings have been linked to one of the biggest names on the trade market for weeks, but it appears the Jonathan Taylors of the world my cost to...
articles.body:
Six days. That is all the time the Minnesota Vikings have left to reshape their roster before the NFL trade deadline hits at 3 p.m. CT on Nov. 10, and one name has followed them around for weeks: Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.

The interest has been real. The Colts opened the door to a Taylor trade on Halloween, and earlier this week Minnesota was named first among the handful of teams leading the chase for his services. The Vikings are 6-1 , but their run game sits at 113.9 yards per game and 4.0 yards per carry, good for 17th and 22nd in the NFL respectively.

Vikings + Jonathan Taylor trade rumors losing steam?

Of course, wanting an elite asset and actually paying for one are two very different things. On Wednesday, Dan Graziano (ESPN) shared what he is hearing about Minnesota's plans at the position.

Minnesota has looked around at running backs, but it doesn't sound as if the Vikings are in position to take on much salary. If they make an addition to help their running game, it might just as easily be an interior offensive lineman or a blocking tight end. And the Packers have checked in on running backs ( Josh Jacobs ' situation remains a major question mark ) as well as offensive linemen. All four teams would occupy playoff spots if the season were to end right now, and I expect them all to be at least somewhat active. In some cases, they'll be competing for the same players. Dan Graziano – ESPN

Minnesota has looked around at running backs, but it doesn't sound as if the Vikings are in position to take on much salary. If they make an addition to help their running game, it might just as easily be an interior offensive lineman or a blocking tight end. And the Packers have checked in on running backs ( Josh Jacobs ' situation remains a major question mark ) as well as offensive linemen. All four teams would occupy playoff spots if the season were to end right now, and I expect them all to be at least somewhat active. In some cases, they'll be competing for the same players.

Money is the first problem. Minnesota has just $5.84 million in cap space, and Taylor is signed through 2028 after a two-year, $44 million extension this offseason. Any deal for him is a multi-year commitment, not a rental.

The asking price is the second. In the same ESPN piece, executives valued Taylor at a second-round pick plus another pick, and the Colts could be holding out for the equivalent of a first.

Other insiders saying same mostly the same as Graziano

Graziano isn't the only one questioning whether general manager Nolan Teasley will go that far. Tom Pelissero (The Ringer) reported on Oct. 31 that the Colts already turned down a 2027 second-round pick plus an additional pick.

Pelissero also reported last week on KFAN, like Graziano today at ESPN, that the Vikings are unlikely to splurge for a running back (like Jonathan Taylor ). The cost is just too high.

More than likely, Teasley doesn't want to dedicate the cap or the draft pick compensation to get a deal done for Taylor, and the Wilfs' probably don't want to spend the cash, which is even more than the cap hits.

On Monday, while The Athletic's Alec Lewis wouldn't rule out a blockbuster running back trade, he too has questions surrounding the fiduciary aspects of what that trade would look like.

"Jonathan Taylor is owed upwards of $16 million if he's on a team's roster in 2027. Then that bumps up to around $17 million if he's on the roster in 2028. Now, you might be saying, 'Well, you could just rent him and cut him,' but you're not going to rent him for a second-round pick plus and then just cut him a year later. That's not serviceable." Alec Lewis – The Alec Lewis Show

"Jonathan Taylor is owed upwards of $16 million if he's on a team's roster in 2027. Then that bumps up to around $17 million if he's on the roster in 2028. Now, you might be saying, 'Well, you could just rent him and cut him,' but you're not going to rent him for a second-round pick plus and then just cut him a year later. That's not serviceable."

What the MN Vikings might do at trade deadline instead

If the Vikings do stay out of the Taylor sweepstakes, and the backfield continues to feature an aging Aaron Jones and Jordan Mason, who returned from IR on Oct. 24 but is not trustworthy in pass pro, which is why DeeJay Dallas got a bunch of snaps in Week 9.

If they avoid adding a running back, they could help themselves with moree talent on the interior offensive line or a new blocking tight end to replace the injured Josh Oliver. They could make moves like that for much cheaper than adding a high-end running back.

Passing on Jonathan Taylor would also leave him on the board for the rest of the NFC North. The Green Bay Packers have checked in on running backs and make a ton of sense. Not landing Taylor would be one thing. His landing in Green Bay would be something else.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk files for reinstatement, plans to report to 49ers. What are team's options?
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has filed paperwork with the NFL to be reinstated and plans to report to the team's facility in Santa Clara o...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers wide receiver who has been a handful is finally forcing his employer's hand.

Brandon Aiyuk, the All-Pro wideout who has spent the past 10-plus months on the 49ers' reserve/left squad list, has filed paperwork with the NFL to be reinstated and plans to report to the team's facility in Santa Clara on Friday afternoon, ESPN reported.

Aiyuk's return will force the 49ers to make a move: They can release Aiyuk or attempt to trade him before the league's trade deadline Tuesday. Another potential option - keeping him - isn't viewed as an option by the team's chief decision-makers.

General manager John Lynch has said Aiyuk has played his last snap with the 49ers. In September, amid a rash of wide receiver injuries, head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked if he'd consider a reunion with Aiyuk. His response: "No."

As far as trading Aiyuk, it's unlikely the 49ers will have a strong market for his services.

Aiyuk, 28, hasn't played in the NFL since Oct. 20, 2024, when he tore multiple ligaments in his right knee and there are questions about how well Aiyuk rehabbed an injury that Lynch termed "catastrophic." The 49ers voided Aiyuk's remaining contract guarantees last year when he didn't participate in mandatory rehab sessions.

Aiyuk's newly hired agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN that his client was "healthy and ready to get back on the field."

Aiyuk has also torpedoed his trade value with his behavior. Shanahan said he didn't see him during the final two months of the 2025 regular season, a period during which he didn't respond to teammates and coaches.

Aiyuk ended his public silence on his in-limbo career in early June with an Instagram video in which he termed the 49ers "female dogs" and "little boys" who were "scared" to play against him once they let him go.

It began a series of summer social-media posts in which Aiyuk made his distaste for Lynch and Shanahan evident. After Shanahan suffered significant injuries in a car wreck in July, Aiyuk tastelessly wrote: "You can't win the race if you crash out."

An arrest warrant had been issued for Aiyuk, according to a report in June, because he was wanted on a misdemeanor speeding charge. In December, Aiyuk had posted a video in which he was captured driving 69 mph in a 40 mph zone as he passed Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara.

In July, after he'd publicly campaigned to join the Commanders, who employ QB Jayden Daniels, his friend and Arizona State teammate, Aiyuk announced he'd purchased a $10 million home near Washington's facility in Ashburn, Va. A day later, Aiyuk, wearing a Commanders hat, urged fans to purchase Commanders tickets.

The 49ers were content to observe from a distance. As long as Aiyuk remained on the reserve/left squad list, he didn't take up a roster spot, the 49ers weren't paying him and they didn't incur a dead-money salary cap charge that would be triggered by his exit.

Aiyuk never tried to force the 49ers' hand by showing up for work during the offseason program or training camp and parted with his agent, Ryan Williams. That, coupled with his online behavior, raised questions about his desire to play in the NFL again.

articles.title: Tez Johnson’s past involved drugs, theft, and street warfare before Bo Nix’s parents brought the Tampa Bay Buccaneers WR home
articles.summary: Tez Johnson’s father killed himself when Tez was an infant.
articles.body: Tez Johnson’s father killed himself when Tez was an infant. His mother, Shamika Posey, raised him with his brothers, Kevontae and Keywone, and their sister, Keynila.At times, he had no bed to sleep in and no food to eat. He often didn’t go home after school. Instead, he went to places he shouldn’t have gone. He admitted to being involved with drugs, theft, and street warfare in a recent interview with The Athletic’s Dan Pompei.If someone wanted to get into a fight, he would be the first one to be called. He wanted to become a mixed martial artist. But his story was being written elsewhere in Pinson.How Bo Nix’s family gave Tez Johnson a second chanceTez Johnson’s mother, Shamika Posey, sought stability, so she moved to subsidized housing in Pinson. That’s where Bo Nix met Tez Johnson. Bo was transferring to Pinson, while his father, Patrick Nix, was the head football coach at Pinson Valley High School.When Bo and Tez played together, Bo believed that something was special about Tez. But before they could transpire into something big, Tez’s mother wanted to send him to a juvenile detention center.Thank God, Bo’s father, the head football coach in Pinson at the time, saw Tez run routes and catch every ball thrown his way. Thank God, the Pinson principal asked Patrick to join the meeting with Tez’s mother.After four hours of discussion, the Nixes decided to host Tez for a night or two, hoping to ease his home stress. Tez felt uneasy walking into a family so different from him.Krista Nix, the mother of the Nix house, gave him two rules: tell her where he was going and say good night before bed. Those two nights that Tez spent at Nixes turned to two weeks, then two months, and the rest is history.Could Bo Nix reunite with Tez Johnson in the NFLBo Nix and Tez Johnson played together in high school and college. They even won a 6A state championship under Bo’s father, coach Patrick Nix. Unfortunately, they couldn’t play together in the NFL. But their love for each other remained eternal.They have stayed connected through calls, messages, and FaceTime. Tez hopes he eventually gets to play with his brother in the NFL too. Their gridiron story is of belonging, support, and a second chance. Isn’t that what Bo Nix needs now? Someone to stabilize his Denver Broncos wins.He’s had six wins and two losses so far into the 2026 NFL season. And he’s leading the AFC West division well above the Patrick Mahomes-led Kansas City Chiefs. But still, to shut down the critiques, he needs his gridiron weapon - Tez Johnson!Could there be a trade from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers? Remains to be ascertained…Krista and Patrick Nix travel miles to support both sonsThe distance from Denver to Tampa Bay is about 1,515 miles. It takes 33 hours of driving and 3.5 hours of flight to cover the distance.But for Bo Nix and Tez Johnson’s parents, Krista and Patrick Nix, it’s nothing. Their sons play for different teams - Bo plays for the Denver Broncos as their NFL quarterback, while Tez plays for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as their wide receiver.There are four game-day timing overlaps this 2026 season - Weeks 2, 4, 11, and 14 - when the Broncos and the Buccaneers have the same kickoff time or just hours apart. Despite this, Krista and Patrick Nix support both their sons.According to MLFootball, the parents reportedly travel across the country every week to cheer for both players, ensuring neither son misses out on family support despite playing for different franchises at different schedules.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Vikings projected to land Big Ten QB in new 2027 NFL Mock Draft
articles.summary: Jayden Maiava is an interesting quarterback prospect in the 2027 class and the Vikings get him in a new mock draft.
articles.body:
The 2027 NFL Draft will take place in Washington, D.C. next year. In that draft, the Vikings still have their first-round pick, but a lot could happen in the next 7 months. Before then, though, there will be plenty of speculation and buildup about the team, and who they may add through the draft in a class many are calling one of generational wealth.

CBS Sports' Ryan Wilson recently released the latest 2027 NFL mock draft of the cycle, which has the team going with star quarterback Jayden Maiava. The USC quarterback is coming off the biggest win of his college career over the Ohio State Buckeyes in Week 9.

He explains the pick, writing, "I've been a big Maiava fan since last season. And I love the idea of a rhythm, pocket passer playing in KOC's offense. He's not going to blow you away with his physical tools but he does a lot of things at a very high level."

Maiava is a fun quarterback who has played in some pass-friendly systems. Through it all, his arm talent has never lacked, and it makes him a prospect that could be a lot of fun to develop under Kevin O'Connell.

articles.title: New Jets Rumors on Will McDonald IV Trade Stance Amid Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson Buzz
articles.summary: Amid a 2-6 start for the New York Jets, Will McDonald IV's status leading up to the trade deadline is being monitored by opposing teams.
articles.body:
Amid a 2-6 start for the New York Jets, Will McDonald IV's status leading up to the trade deadline is being monitored by opposing teams.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , even though the Jets "do not plan" on trading McDonald right now, teams looking for pass-rush help might "make an attractive offer" if they miss out on another player at that spot before the Nov. 10 deadline.

Despite being on pace for their 11th consecutive losing season, the Jets are actually in a great position to not do anything at the trade deadline and still be fine going forward.

Garrett Wilson was a name that had been popping up in trade rumors, but there's no indication the Jets are looking to move their star wide receiver. A Breece Hall trade hasn't been as forcefully dismissed as Wilson, but it still seems like a long shot.

The primary reason for optimism around the Jets right now is the 2027 draft in which they will have three first-round picks. Based on the current standings , all three of those selections are in the top 10, starting at No. 4 with the pick they are owed from the Indianapolis Colts from the Sauce Gardner trade.

New York seems to have prioritized players like Wilson and Hall as long-term building blocks by signing both players to contract extensions. Wilson is under contract through the 2030 season; Hall is signed through 2028.

McDonald, a first-round pick in the 2023 draft, has not received an extension despite being eligible to sign one since after last season. The Jets did pick up the fifth-year option on his rookie contract that will keep him under team control through 2027.

While McDonald has not developed into a star player, he is a solid rotational pass-rusher. The 27-year-old has 53 quarterback hits, 27 tackles for loss and 24.5 sacks in 55 career games.

Given the current trade market for pass-rushers is largely centered around an older player like Khalil Mack or an expensive player like Josh Sweat, who still has two more years remaining on his four-year, $76.4 million deal with the Arizona Cardinals, someone like McDonald could be a solid alternative because of his age and lack of a long-term financial commitment.

articles.title: Tom Brady: Seven-time Super Bowl champion returns to New England Patriots as broadcaster for first time at Foxboro
articles.summary: Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady to feature as commentator as New England Patriots take on Green Bay Packers at home in Foxboro this Sunday; watch the 2026 NFL season live on Sky Sports, including every minute of the playoffs
articles.body:
The seven-time Super Bowl champion will serve as colour commentator for Fox Sports at Gillette Stadium for the first time when the Patriots face the Green Bay Packers, live on Sky Sports NFL from 9.25pm.

Brady appeared at nine Super Bowls and won six across a historic 20-year career with the Patriots, accompanying Bill Belichick to forge one of the NFL's greatest dynasties.

"I get to be there to watch it in person in front of a very friendly home crowd, I'm very excited," Brady said on The Herd with Colin Cowherd.

"It'll be certainly emotional. I mean, every inch of that stadium, I've been through so many times.

"From the locker rooms to the media rooms to the field. Just so many memorable plays in that stadium. Big games, championship games and rivalry games, division-clinching games."

Brady, drafted with the 199th overall pick at the 2000 NFL Draft, won three MVP awards while passing for 74,571 yards and 541 touchdowns before leaving in 2019.

He subsequently joined the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, where he won his seventh Super Bowl ring in his first season with the team.

"To be back there and to really understand what that Patriot organisation is all about and to convey that to the fans in a way where I'm not talking about myself, I'm really talking about this awesome program that's been built," Brady continued.

"And the Patriots just always seem to do things the right way."

The Patriots enter Sunday's game 5-3 and second in the AFC East as they strive to remain in Super Bowl contention after falling at the final hurdle against the Seattle Seahawks in February's season finale.

It awaits as a matchup of the two franchises with the winningest records in the NFL since the Packers beat the Patriots at Super Bowl XXXI at the end of the 1996 season. The Patriots have built a league-best record of 327-166 over the 30 years since that game, followed by Green Bay's regular-season return of 310-180-3.

New England won all six of their Super Bowls in that time and reached the playoffs in 22 of 30 years, while the Packers clinched two Championships and have also made the playoffs on 22 occasions in the last three decades.

articles.title: Mack Hollins Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Patriots WR's Return Timeline Ahead of Packers Game
articles.summary: The New England Patriots may be getting much-needed reinforcements for their injury-depleted receiving corps.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots may be getting much-needed reinforcements for their injury-depleted receiving corps.

Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins is set to return to practice, NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport reported on Wednesday. Hollins has missed the last four games after being placed on the injured reserved list with a calf injury. A return to practice opens a 21-day window for Hollins to be activated, but he could also make his return as soon as Sunday against the Green Bay Packers.

Hollins reeled in 15 catches for 209 yards through four games prior to his injury, but his value to the team goes beyond his statistical production. The 33-year-old wide receiver has excelled as a blocker on running plays and has been a steady veteran presence in the locker room.

The Patriots has struggled to find consistent production from their wide receivers this season. Wide receivers A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs headlined the Patriots' offseason acquisitions, but both players have missed significant time due to injuries. New England also parted ways with wide receivers Stefon Diggs and Kayshon Boutte, who led the team in yards and touchdowns last season, respectively.

The Patriots are entering one of the toughest stretches on their schedule, and Hollins would immediately bolster a wide receiver room that dwindled down to just DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism III last week.

New England will host the Packers at Gillette Stadium on Sunday before traveling to Munich for an international matchup against the Detroit Lions.

articles.title: New Eagles Rumors on Potential of Rebuild at NFL Trade Deadline Amid Struggles, Jalen Hurts' Absence
articles.summary: Despite losing six straight games and being without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, the Philadelphia Eagles reportedly aren't planning on phoning it in for the rest of the year.
articles.body:
Despite losing six straight games and being without star quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the season, the Philadelphia Eagles reportedly aren't planning on phoning it in for the rest of the year.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano predicted that the Eagles will not kick off a rebuild by shipping away some of their top players ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline.

"My sense is the Eagles could be trading some players but likely won't engage in a rebuild," Fowler stated. "As one source pointed out, that's not in the Eagles' organizational DNA. We already know they aren't trading running back Saquon Barkley. Look, let's not be naive -- general manager Howie Roseman will take advantage of good value if it's there, and supporting players are surely on the radar. But dealing big names would be a mild surprise."

Fowler went on to name Philadelphia defensive tackle Moro Ojomo as a player who is generating "real interest" on the trade market, with the Jacksonville Jaguars leading the pursuit. Still, there's some skepticism about whether the team would make any major changes.

Graziano agreed that he doesn't "anticipate a big selloff" and outlined the more likely scenarios for the Eagles.

"First off, they're very cap-leveraged because of the way they structure their veteran contracts, and trading some of them would make that worse with dead money hits accelerating into this season," Graziano explained. "If the Eagles trade away players, I'd be looking at guys like [Riq] Woolen, WR Hollywood Brown and maybe, maybe tight end Dallas Goedert for the right offer. If they're adding, I would expect it to be players who are signed beyond this season."

The Eagles (2-6) will try to end their losing streak on Sunday against the New York Giants (4-2-1), and their performance in that game could determine their outlook for the trade deadline.

articles.title: New Raiders Rumors on Ashton Jeanty's 'Wake-Up Call' After Mike Washington Jr.'s Increased Usage
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are hoping second-year running back Ashton Jeanty will see his limited usage in last Sunday's win at the New York Jets as a "wake-up call," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Wednesday.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are hoping second-year running back Ashton Jeanty will see his limited usage in last Sunday's win at the New York Jets as a "wake-up call," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Wednesday.

Mike Washington Jr. recorded 25 carries for 83 yards in Week 8, while Jeanty saw a career-low two touches for nine yards.

If this doesn't spark any changes from Jeanty, Graziano reported the Raiders are "content to distribute the carries in Washington's favor moving forward, as he offers a more explosive element in the run game right now."

Graziano also noted the decision to turn to Washington over Jeanty could be seen a reflection of strong roster influence from head coach Klint Kubiak, who was hired after Jeanty was selected with the No. 6 pick of the 2025 draft.

Kubiak told reporters earlier this week the decision to give Washington more touches against the Jets was his call. He also said Jeanty's role reduction wasn't related to his pregame comments disparaging the effort of the Jets' run defense.

"He's gonna be a huge part of our run game moving forward. We just wanted to give Mike a few more opportunities today," Kubiak said Sunday about Jeanty. "I think both of those guys are gonna be a huge part of our rushing and passing success moving forward."

Jeanty suffered a sprained ankle during practice in late August but was available to record a season-high 23 carries in Week 1.

According to Graziano, the Raiders felt Jeanty had limitations from that injury early in the season but is now "at a point where they want to see him play better."

Jeanty had recorded 106 carries for 328 yards with one touchdown heading into last weekend's matchup against the Jets.

He had also made 34 receptions, including three touchdown catches, while ranking first among running backs with 312 receiving yards. Jeanty again played a key role in his team's pass game during Sunday's win in New York.

The Raiders are preparing for a matchup Sunday at the San Francisco 49ers against a run defense that has so far ranked among the most effective in the NFL this season.

Even if Jeanty sees more touches this weekend, Kubiak has indicated he could be considering splitting the backfield more between Jeanty and Washington when the Week 9 matchup kicks off at 4:25 p.m. ET in Santa Clara.

articles.title: Garrett Wilson Injured, Latest Updates on Jets WR's Status vs. Chiefs After Concussion
articles.summary: New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson's status for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs is up in the air.
articles.body:
New York Jets wide receiver Garrett Wilson's status for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs is up in the air.

Jets head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Wednesday that Wilson has been placed in concussion protocol.

It's unclear exactly when Wilson was injured. He played the entirety of Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Las Vegas Raiders, finishing with 83 yards on six receptions.

Wednesday marks the first day of practice going into Week 9 for the Jets.

NFL rules require players to go through a five-step process to be fully cleared from concussion protocol. The return-to-participation protocol includes supervised limited stretching and balancing; then aerobic exercises; football-specific exercises; non-contact training drills; and full football activity after receiving clearance from a team doctor.

Wilson has started each of New York's first eight games this season. He was limited to seven games during the 2025 campaign due to knee injuries.

The 26-year-old has never missed a game in his NFL career due to a concussion. He is on pace for the best season of his career with 43 receptions, 527 receiving yards and three touchdowns.

New York has lost six of its first eight games this season, including three straight. Five of the Jets' six losses have come by seven points or fewer.

The Jets will look to end their losing skid against the Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium. They haven't beaten Kansas City since December 2017.

If Wilson is unable to play, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr. will be the top two receivers for the Jets.

articles.title: Patriots' Robert Kraft Among Finalists to Be Elected to Pro Football HOF as Contributor
articles.summary: For the second straight year, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft will have the chance to earn a spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
articles.body:
For the second straight year, New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft will have the chance to earn a spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

On Wednesday, Kraft was announced as one of five contributor nominees for the Hall of Fame class of 2027, along with Ralph Hay, Virginia McCaskey, Doug Williams and John Wooten. Kraft was also a contributor finalist in the class of 2026, but he ultimately was not selected for entry.

The five finalists were selected from an original field of 42 nominees. Members of the Contributor Subcommittee will hold a virtual meeting on Nov. 17 to select one finalist to be considered by the full Selection Committee. Kraft was chosen as the contributor finalist last year before falling short.

The 50 voters each pick three of the five finalists among contributors, coaches and senior players who last appeared in a game in 2000 or earlier, with 40 votes required for one to three nominees to be inducted alongside three to five modern era players from a group of 15 finalists.

Last year, Kraft happened to be joined on the ballot by former Patriots head coach Bill Belichick, but neither earned an induction. Roger Craig, Ken Anderson and L.C. Greenwood were the senior player finalists, with Craig getting the nod. The former running back was enshrined alongside quarterback Drew Brees, wide receiver Larry Fitzgerald, linebacker Luke Kuechly and kicker Adam Vinatieri.

Kraft has overseen 11 Super Bowl appearances and six titles in his 31 seasons at the helm of the Patriots. He is also a key member of several NFL owners' committees. While his impact is unquestioned, it remains to be seen if voters make him a Hall of Famer this time around.

articles.title: Lions' Jack Campbell Provides Injury Update in Statement, Remains 'Very Optimistic' About Recovery
articles.summary: Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell said Wednesday he's "incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time" while recovering from a serious neck injury.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell said Wednesday he's "incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time" while recovering from a serious neck injury.

"I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body," he said in a statement released by the team. "I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better."

Campbell went to tackle Minnesota Vikings tight end T.J. Hockenson during last Sunday's 19-15 win. His upper body bent backward in an unnatural way, and he remained motionless on the turf.

Trainers placed Campbell on a backboard and carted him off the field.

The team followed up Monday to say the 26-year-old remained hospitalized and showed "positive" progress.

A first-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft, Campbell is in his fourth season with Detroit. He was a Pro Bowler and All-Pro in 2025 after finishing with 176 combined tackles and three forced fumbles. The Lions rewarded him with a four-year, $81 million extension.

To open the season, Campbell has 57 tackles through seven games.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors Reveal Vikings' Reaction to J.J. McCarthy Winning 1st Start with Giants After Trade
articles.summary: The Minnesota Vikings may have moved on from J.J. McCarthy, but they're still rooting for their former quarterback to succeed.
articles.body:
The Minnesota Vikings may have moved on from J.J. McCarthy, but they're still rooting for their former quarterback to succeed.

The Vikings were "very happy" to see McCarthy thrive in his first start with the New York Giants, ESPN's Dan Graziano reported on Wednesday.

"[The] Vikings people I spoke to were very happy for quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who thrived in his first start as a Giant after being traded away from the team that drafted him 10th in 2024," Graziano wrote.

McCarthy was traded to New York after Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending injury in September. The third-year quarterback initially stepped in for the Giants after head coach John Harbaugh benched starter Jameis Winston against the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. McCarthy finished the game with 11 completions on 21 pass attempts for 243 passing yards with a touchdown and an interception.

Although the Giants suffered a 34-27 loss to the Saints, McCarthy earned the start against the Houston Texans and pulled out a 27-21 overtime win with 20 completions on 28 pass attempts for 252 yards and no turnovers.

Minnesota selected McCarthy with the No. 10 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft after failing to find consistent success with veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins. The Vikings initially signed Sam Darnold to serve as a stopgap quarterback during McCarthy's rookie season. Although Darnold led Minnesota to a 14-3 record while the rookie was sidelined with a meniscus injury, the Vikings still elected to move on from Darnold and rolled into the 2025 season with McCarthy as their starting quarterback. The results were underwhelming, and Minnesota parted ways with the embattled quarterback after he was beat out for the starting role by veteran Kyler Murray.

Perhaps most notably, the Vikings are aware that McCarthy has the potential to make them look bad.

"They also recognize they have a chance to look bad if McCarthy plays well for the Giants and Kyler Murray doesn't get things going in Minnesota, but everyone agrees it was time for a scenery change," Graziano wrote.

The 2024 draft has the potential to be a historic quarterback class, but so far, McCarthy has been the least successful of the six quarterbacks selected in the top 12 picks that year. There is still time for that to change, however. Graziano noted that the coaching staffs for both teams have praised McCarthy's maturity.

"Minnesota coaches told me they believed McCarthy had matured significantly since the start of the 2026 offseason ... and they were happy the team had been able to send him to a place where he had a chance to be successful," Graziano wrote.

McCarthy now has an opportunity to join the list of quarterbacks to thrive after leaving Minnesota. Darnold and Cousins, who the Vikings parted ways with for McCarthy, have both found success elsewhere.

articles.title: Lions' Jack Campbell says he has full movement in lower body, 'encouraged' by progress made during his recovery
articles.summary: The Lions linebacker needed to be carted off and immobilized on a backboard following a multi-player tackle on Sunday.
articles.body:
Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell released a statement Wednesday saying he is "encouraged by the progress" he's made over the past few days after suffering a serious injury on Sunday.

Campbell added that he has full movement of his lower body and is making progress on movement in his upper body.

"My family and I want to sincerely thank everyone for the overwhelming amount of love, prayers, and support we've received over the past few days. It means more to us than words can express," Campbell said in a statement. "I'm incredibly encouraged by the progress I've made in such a short period of time. I have full movement in my lower body, and I'm continuing to make progress with movement in my upper body. I know there's still work ahead, but I remain very optimistic. I'm taking things one day at a time, staying positive, and focusing on getting better. "My faith in God has never been stronger. I know He has a plan for me, and I trust in that plan. I know there may be challenges ahead, but with my faith, my family, and so many people in my corner, I know we'll get through this. "I especially want to thank the athletic trainers and medical personnel who responded and cared for me on the field. I know those were difficult moments, and I'm incredibly grateful for the professionalism, compassion, and care you showed me. The way you handled everything and looked after me when I needed it most is something I'll never forget. From the bottom of my heart, thank you. "I also can't say enough about the incredible care I've received from the medical team at Henry Ford Hospital and the Detroit Lions medical staff. They've been amazing to me and my family throughout this process, and I'm truly grateful for everything they've done. "To my teammates, coaches, and everyone in the Lions organization, I want you to know how much I love and appreciate you. This team is a family to me, and the way everyone has been there for me means everything. I'm proud to be a Detroit Lion and couldn't ask to be surrounded by a better group of people. "One thing I've learned about Detroit is that this city is built on toughness, resilience, and grit. That's exactly how I'm going to approach this challenge. "Please continue to keep me and my family in your prayers. We feel the love, and I can't thank everyone enough. "God is good. My faith is strong. "Jack Campbell"

During the Lions' win over the Minnesota Vikings, Campbell was immobilized on a backboard and needed to be carted off the field following a multi-player tackle in the fourth quarter.

After being tended to by medical personnel, Campbell was surrounded by teammates and was taken off the field and transported to a local hospital. Afterward, Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the linebacker is "being taken care of" but had no additional information about his condition.

The team said Monday that preliminary indications were positive for Campbell. Dan Campbell expressed the same sentiment saying, "It's positive. Your prayers are working; please continue to do that. We'll leave it at that. Just continue to pray for him, but it is positive news on Jack."

articles.title: Jordyn Tyson Returns to Saints Practice, Latest Rumors on WR's Timeline to Make NFL Debut
articles.summary: The New Orleans Saints are getting closer to seeing the debut of their first-round pick. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice on Wednesday, according to Saints reporter Nick Underhill.
articles.body:
The New Orleans Saints are getting closer to seeing the debut of their first-round pick. Saints rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson returned to practice on Wednesday, according to Saints reporter Nick Underhill .

New Orleans selected the Arizona State product with the No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but a hamstring injury landed Tyson on the injured reserve list during training camp.

Saints head coach Kellen Moore told reporters on Monday that the team is still working through a decision on opening Tyson's 21-day return window, which would begin if Tyson makes his return to practice.

Despite having a 2-5 record, the Saints still have the opportunity to make the playoffs in a weak NFC South division.

The Saints could activate Tyson at any point during his window, but a return sooner than later could be crucial to turning their season around. Although the Saints are currently in last place in their division, they are only one win behind the Carolina Panthers for the division lead.

After an opportunity to reset and get healthy during a Week 8 bye, New Orleans will have a chance to get back in the win column Sunday against the Cleveland Browns. The following week, the Saints will face the Panthers at home in a game that could have massive playoff implications. Having Tyson back before then could prove to be significant.

Tyson could help draw some defensive coverage away from star wideout Chris Olave, who is currently on pace to surpass 1,500 receiving yards this season. Olave and third-year wide receiver Devaughn Vele are currently the only two Saints wide receivers with more than 10 catches and 100 receiving yards.

The Saints have the No. 14 ranked scoring offense in large part due to their passing game, but they have struggled to move the ball on the ground and their defense has been porous. Along with Tyson, New Orleans could also see offensive tackle Kelvin Banks and running back Travis Etienne return from injured reserve, which could help improve their rushing attack.

articles.title: Rams' Quentin Lake Rips Justin Herbert for 'Throwing Deli Meat' in Video, 'He's Seeing Ghosts'
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake was less than impressed by what he saw from Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert in his team's 24-9 win.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams safety Quentin Lake was less than impressed by what he saw from Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert in his team's 24-9 win.

Lake said on the St. Brown Podcast that Herbert "was throwing deli meat out there." He added the two-time Pro Bowler looks so shaky in the pocket he's "seeing ghosts."

Coach: Herbert 'Incredibly Uncomfortable'

Herbert went 24-of-32 for 257 yards and two interceptions. Lake was responsible for one of those picks as he jumped an out route by Chargers tight end Charlie Kolar.

Lake's biting assessment of Herbert speaks for itself, and a lot of fans who have watched the Chargers signal-caller probably feel the same way.

Even Herbert's biggest critics couldn't have predicted how badly the wheels would fall off for him. His 10 interceptions are the most in the NFL, and he's dead last in QBR (32.6) among qualified players, per ESPN.com .

"He doesn't seem comfortable in the offense," one AFC executive said to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . "I don't know that it's a great schematic fit for his talents. He's throwing a lot of picks where he simply isn't seeing defenders. I don't know how it gets better."

Maybe Herbert rediscovers his confidence in the second half of the season, or the Chargers fire offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and install a scheme that better suits him.

Until then, opposing secondaries are relishing their matchups against L.A.

articles.title: Sam Darnold Injured, Latest News on QB's Status and Return Timeline Ahead of Seahawks vs. Cardinals
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will be sidelined with a quad injury for Sunday's matchup against the visiting Arizona Cardinals, head coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.

Darnold is considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald.

Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of Monday's loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald.

Macdonald clarified it is the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action.

Drew Lock is dealing with an elbow injury but if available is slated to start with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals, Macdonald said.

The Seahawks don't currently have any other quarterbacks on the roster. Macdonald didn't rule out the possibility of adding another signal caller ahead of Sunday's game.

Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions.

Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold.

The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos.

Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs.

Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can."

As of Wednesday, Macdonald said Lock was "able to throw" but that his capacity would be determined during practice this week.

Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks.

The Seahawks (4-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (6-1).

A win this week over the Cardinals (3-5) would increase the defending champions' playoff odds to 54 percent, while a loss would drop the team to 29 percent, according to NFL Next Gen Stats .

How much participation Lock sees in practice this week could provide an early indication as to whether Milroe will be making his first NFL start in a crucial divisional matchup this weekend.

articles.title: Joe Milton Named Eagles QB1, Tanner McKee Benched Ahead of Giants Matchup Amid Jalen Hurts' Absence
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the New York Giants, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the New York Giants, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo .

Philly is hopeful Milton can help snap a six-game losing skid before the team heads into its Week 10 bye.

The third-year signal-caller has thrown for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions in five NFL appearances.

Milton has long drawn praise for his raw tools but lacked the accuracy to be a consistent starter in college. The fact he's on his third pro team illustrates how his game hasn't evolved much.

According to Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer , the Eagles think Milton's mobility can be an asset against the Giants.

If nothing else, they know Tanner McKee isn't the answer with Jalen Hurts potentially sidelined for the remainder of the year. In his three starts after replacing Hurts, McKee had 638 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions, and he completed 63.2 percent of his passes.

The Eagles are going nowhere fast. They have the worst record in the NFC (2-6), and Hurts' absence means there's little hope of dramatically improving the rest of the way.

Maybe Milton isn't much better than McKee as the starter. There's no real downside to giving him a shot.

articles.title: Packers' Micah Parsons cleared to return to practice, takes part in individual drills as he begins ramp-up
articles.summary: It's been close to 11 months since Parsons tore his ACL and meniscus in his left knee last season.
articles.body:
An NFL Network report surfaced over the weekend that the Green Bay Packers and star pass rusher Micah Parsons are targeting their Thanksgiving Eve road game against the Los Angeles Rams for his return to game action .

On Wednesday, Parsons took a significant step toward making that holiday comeback. Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that Parsons was cleared to return to practice, and the sack artist took part in individual drills, beginning his ramp-up.

While Parsons is only a limited practice participant at this point, his first practice since he tore his ACL and meniscus in his left knee more than 320 days ago is of course notable.

It's been close to 11 months since the Packers played a game with the four-time All-Pro.

"I think it's great," LaFleur said Wednesday, when asked what Parsons being back on the practice field does for the group's morale. "I think it's been a long time coming, and he's put a lot of effort and work into this. To get him back out there will be a big boost for our team."

LaFleur later added: "A lot of people in our building have done a great job with him, and we'll just see where it goes."

Parsons' 21-day window to be activated from the physically unable to perform list is now open.

A reporter inquired Monday if the Packers are entering that window anticipating the 27-year-old Parsons will need need all 21 days.

"I would just say, like everything around here, it's pretty fluid in terms of how he responds and just the progress he's going to hopefully continue to make leading up to when he's available," LaFleur said.

He then noted: "If I had to bet on it, it's going to be more toward the longer end than the shorter end."

As captured by multiple reporters on site Wednesday, Parsons was wearing a sleeve on his left knee while going through his first drills back.

Parsons' absence was sorely missed down the stretch of the 2025 campaign. After he suffered the injury in a Week 15 road loss to the Denver Broncos on Dec. 14 , Green Bay went on to drop four more games in a row to end the season, including their wild-card matchup versus the rival Chicago Bears in the playoffs.

This season, the 5-3 Packers' defense has managed without Parsons on the field. Led by first-year Green Bay defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon, the unit ranks 10th in the NFL with 20.5 points per game allowed. Plus, it's tied for sixth in the league with 22 sacks.

Adding Parsons back into the fold should take Green Bay to an even higher level of play on that side of the ball.

"I mean, he's a generational talent," LaFleur said Wednesday. "He definitely flips the favor of the field into your court in regards to his ability to win his 1-on-1s. And I think, like we saw a year ago, the thing that impressed me most about him was his impact in the run game as well. So he's a dominant force."

In 14 games last time around, Parsons stacked 12.5 sacks. By that point of the season, he had accounted for a third of Green Bay's pressures, according to Next Gen Stats. His 20.7% pressure rate in 2025 was the third best of his career, per NGS.

It was his first go-around with the Packers, who acquired the 2021 No. 12 overall pick just 10 days before their season opener. The former Dallas Cowboys standout signed a four-year, $188 million deal with Green Bay, including a reported $136 million of guaranteed money , that made him, at the time, the highest-paid non-quarterback in NFL history.

Gannon has found success this season with aggressive play-calling. But, soon enough, he should have Parsons at his disposal, affording him more opportunities to create pressure with just a four-man rush.

For now, the Packers are still taking things one day at a time with Parsons.

That said, LaFleur clarified Wednesday that the edge defender has been "cleared to go full go in regards to what he's doing out there." On Wednesday, that was individual drills.

"Hopefully he'll be ready to go sooner than later," LaFleur said.

articles.title: Eagles QB Joe Milton will reportedly make first career start in Week 9 vs. Giants
articles.summary: This will be the first start of Milton's NFL career.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles will start quarterback Joe Milton this weekend against the New York Giants, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Milton takes over for Tanner McKee, who was called on to fill in for quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is out indefinitely due to blood clots in his lungs .

This will be Milton's first career NFL start, and his first game action for Philadelphia since the franchise signed him away from the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Oct. 16.

Milton, 26, spent his collegiate career between Michigan and Tennessee from 2018 to 2023. The Patriots drafted the quarterback in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft.

He hasn't had many opportunities to play, but when he has, he's impressed with his arm strength.

Milton took the field for the first time during Week 18 of the 2024 season, coming on for Drake Maye. The quarterback threw for 241 yards and a touchdown, plus 16 yards and another score on the ground. After the season, the Patriots traded him to the Cowboys.

In his lone full season in Dallas, Milton appeared in four games. Overall, he had 183 passing yards, a passing touchdown, two interceptions and 50 rushing yards on five carries.

The Cowboys waived Milton this fall when Sam Howell earned the backup quarterback role, but Dallas signed him to the practice squad.

Philadelphia drafted McKee in the sixth round of the 2023 NFL Draft. He has been mainly used as a third-string quarterback, including this year. McKee began the season behind Hurts and Andy Dalton, but the Eagles released Dalton before Hurts was injured and promoted McKee to backup.

He has played in three games this year, and Philadelphia has lost all three. McKee has thrown for 638 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.

The Eagles are 2-6 and in last place in the NFC East. Philadelphia has a chance for a much-needed win this weekend against a 4-2-1 New York squad that currently leads the division.

After this weekend's game against the Giants, Philly has its bye week. Then, starting in Week 11, the Eagles play the Pittsburgh Steelers, Cowboys, Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts.

articles.title: Jacoby Brissett Traded to Ravens Amid Lamar Jackson Injury, Latest NFL Rumors on Deal With Cardinals
articles.summary: After losing star quarterback Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley to a toe injury, the Baltimore Ravens reportedly made a much-needed addition.
articles.body:
After losing star quarterback Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury and backup Tyler Huntley to a toe injury, the Baltimore Ravens reportedly made a much-needed addition.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, the Ravens are finalizing a trade to acquire veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. The deal is expected to be completed this weekend.

Schefter added that the deal won't be finalized in time for Brissett to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Thursday Night Football , leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the likely starter. Brissett will be expected to make his debut in Week 10 on Monday Night Football against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Schefter reported that Huntley is expected to miss the remainder of the season due to turf toe, which will require surgery. The bad news came after Jackson was placed on injured reserve due to thumb surgery, ruling him out for at least a month.

Brissett started Arizona's first eight games but was benched on Sunday in favor of Gardner Minshew II, who led the team to a 33-30 overtime win over the Dallas Cowboys. Rookie Carson Beck was named the backup, and he was relegated to QB3. The 33-year-old has completed 63.3 percent of his passes for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions this season.

At 4-4, the Ravens still have time to save their season and chase a playoff spot. Adding Brissett gives Baltimore a reliable signal-caller who can steady the ship until Jackson is able to return to the lineup.

articles.title: Ravens reportedly acquire QB Jacoby Brissett from Cardinals to make up for Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries
articles.summary: The trade is expected to be completed this weekend, so Brissett will not play tomorrow against the Jaguars.
articles.body:
The Baltimore Ravens are acquiring veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Brissett will add experience to a quarterback room that will be without starter Lamar Jackson and backup Tyler Huntley for the foreseeable future.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the trade is expected to be completed this coming weekend. That means the Ravens will not have Brissett for Thursday night's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. Baltimore is set to start undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano. Austin Reed and Kedon Slovis will back him up, and both signed with the Ravens earlier this week.

Schefter reported that Brissett is expected to start for Baltimore in its following game against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10's edition of "Monday Night Football."

Baltimore will acquire Brissett for his experience. The Ravens' current quarterback room has zero career passing touchdowns, while starting running back Derrick Henry has four.

Brissett signed with the Cardinals this summer after holding out for a better contract. He has led Arizona to a 3-5 record this season, and has 1,719 passing yards, 10 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. The veteran quarterback was benched late in the third quarter of last weekend's game against the Dallas Cowboys. Arizona trailed 17-3 before Gardner Minshew led the Cardinals to a comeback overtime win.

On Tuesday, it was announced Minshew would start in Week 9 for Arizona against the Seattle Seahawks.

While Ravens fans can get excited for the experienced QB heading to their team, they will have to wait a week to see him in action. That means Fagnano will lead the offense in the meantime, as Jackson was added to injured reserve with a thumb injury , and Huntley was diagnosed with turf toe, which is expected to end his season.

In relief last week, Fagnano completed 10-of-21 passes for 91 yards and an interception. Fagnano also ran the ball three times for 3 yards.

articles.title: Shedeur Sanders Reacts to Browns QB1 Buzz in Video Amid Deshaun Watson Injury
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker last Sunday. Shedeur Sanders is next in line to start if Watson cannot go this Sunday at the New Orleans Saints.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson is in concussion protocol after taking a helmet-to-helmet hit from Pittsburgh Steelers safety Jaquan Brisker last Sunday. Shedeur Sanders is next in line to start if Watson cannot go this Sunday at the New Orleans Saints.

On Wednesday, Sanders spoke with reporters.

"The same way I've been preparing every week, no different," Sanders said when asked how he is preparing this week as the potential starter.

Sanders also added this: "Well first, I just want to thank the whole coaching staff, [general manager Andrew Berry] and everybody in the organization for giving me another chance to be here for this season and everything. Last year, I was able to see what I need to see, feel different things during the games and understand what I need to get better at. So then going into this offseason, we worked on that and training camp of course and this offseason, and overall I'm just excited for this opportunity."

Sanders appears ready for the moment if he plays.

"I'm comfortable with the ball in my hands in general," Sanders said in part. "Just go in there, do what I have to do. Play the long game, win everything, and just be excited to get out there."

Sanders played in eight games (seven starts) for the Browns last season. He completed 56.6 percent of his passes for seven touchdowns (10 interceptions) and 1,400 yards (6.6 yards per attempt).

Sanders, a fifth-round selection in the 2025 NFL draft, initially sat as Joe Flacco and then Dillon Gabriel started for the team. The former Colorado star got called into action when Gabriel entered concussion protocol. Sanders then started the final seven games.

This year, Sanders and Deshaun Watson, who missed the back half of 2024 with a torn Achilles and then sat all of 2025 after suffering a re-rupture of the same Achilles , were in a QB1 battle. Watson won and has done well, completing 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards (7.25 yards per attempt), seven touchdowns and three interceptions. Cleveland has gone 5-3 thus far.

Sanders could very well be the starter on Sunday, though, in a crucial game for the Browns as they fight for the AFC North title or an AFC postseason spot at worst. Kickoff on Sunday is set for 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Sam Darnold ruled out for Week 9 game vs. Cardinals due to quad injury
articles.summary: Drew Lock is the next man up... though is also dealing with an injury.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks will be without quarterback Sam Darnold for at least one more game during the 2026 season. The quarterback will surprisingly miss the team's Week 9 game against the Arizona Cardinals due to a quad injury, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald announced Wednesday.

It will mark the second time this season Darnold has been ruled out vs. the Cardinals. He missed the Week 2 matchup against the team due to a glute injury.

The news comes after Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards and two touchdowns in a 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears on Monday. Darnold also threw an interception during the contest.

Darnold was able to finish the game and was on the field for the Seahawks' final offensive play of the night. The quarterback, however, picked up the quad injury at some point near the end of the contest, per Macdonald. It's unclear exactly when Darnold sustained the injury.

It wasn't the only injury he dealt with vs. the Bears. Darnold also cracked a rib on the game's second play. That could explain why Darnold struggled with his accuracy during the game. His 50 percent completion percentage was his lowest of the season if you include his 1 for 2 performance in Week 1.

With Darnold out in Week 9, the Seahawks will once again turn to backup Drew Lock … who is also dealing with an injury. Despite an injured elbow that's held him out of the last two games, however, Lock is expected to start against the Cardinals in Week 9.

He was excellent against the team in Week 2, going 19 of 26 for 235 yards and three touchdowns in a 31-7 win . While it initially looked like Lock was in for a longer stint as the team's starter, Darnold was able to return from his glute issue faster than expected, and was able to start for the team in Week 3.

Lock apparently got out of that game unscathed, as his elbow issue didn't pop up on the team's injury report until Week 6, when it was initially ruled a forearm injury. It was classified as an elbow injury ahead of Week 7. Lock was also listed on the team's injury report with an elbow issue ahead of Week 8.

Despite the injury, Lock has been listed as a limited participant in practices over the past three weeks. On the off-chance Lock is unable to go, the Seahawks would be forced to turn to Jalen Milroe.

Darnold's injury comes at an inopportune time for Seattle. Following the team's loss in Week 8, the Seahawks sit at 4-4 on the season. If the playoffs started today, the team would not make the postseason.

Because of that, the Seahawks need to make a second-half push if the team wants to defend its Super Bowl title. While there's still plenty of season left, a loss to the Cardinals in Week 9 would be a significant blow to the team's playoff chances.
