articles.title: NFL: Charlie Smyth to return as starting New Orleans Saints kicker this weekend
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore confirms Charlie Smyth will start as kicker against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore has confirmed Charlie Smyth will start as kicker against the Cleveland Browns on Sunday.

Smyth had been on the Saints' practice squad with Daniel Carlson earning the starting slot for the season, but inconsistent form saw the 31-year-old's contract terminated earlier this week.

On Monday, Moore said he would "evaluate" the situation and at Wednesday's news briefing, he announced Smyth will start against the Browns at the Caesars Superdome this week.

"Charlie will kick this week," he confirmed.

"[There have been] tough decisions. Daniel has made some really big kicks for us - it's just the consistency thing. I just felt this is the best decision for our football team going forward.

"These things are never easy, but Charlie has done this for us at the backend of last year, so he will be ready to go."

Smyth, a former Gaelic footballer from Mayobridge in County Down, made his NFL debut last season but returned to the practice roster after the Saints elected to bring in Carlson for the start of the current campaign after spending five seasons with the Las Vegas Raiders.

Carlson had a success rate of 66% from 12 field goal attempts and his only perfect game with the boot came in September, when he landed three kicks against the Baltimore Ravens.

He made 16 of his 18 extra point attempts for the struggling Saints, who have just two wins from seven games this season, before his contract was terminated on Tuesday.

With the Saints opting not bringing any additional kickers into their squad, Smyth returns to the starting line-up.

The 25-year-old made 12 of 16 field goals and was successful on each of his 13 extra point attempts as a starter last season, after his historic NFL debut last November.

He had a mixed pre-season and dropped back down the practice squad after Carlson was selected to be the Saints' first choice following a kicking competition ahead of the NFL season.

"When guys aren't playing these games, not everyone gets to see all the work they do during the week," Moore said of Smyth's development in the practice squad.

"They still have a plan. Charlie has a plan going into every week [for] how is he going to get better, similar to [quarterback] Tyler Shough when he was on practice squad.

"The guys who don't play on Sunday still have a plan to develop and get better, then opportunities like this present themselves and they are ready."

articles.title: Jaylen Watson to Undergo Surgery on Injury, Latest News on Rams CB's Status and Return Timeline
articles.summary: Los Angeles Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson will undergo surgery on his right shoulder and miss the remainder of the season, per head coach Sean McVay to reporters on Wednesday.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Rams cornerback Jaylen Watson will undergo surgery on his right shoulder and miss the remainder of the season, per head coach Sean McVay to reporters on Wednesday.

Watson initially suffered a dislocated right shoulder in Week 3 against the Denver Broncos. He missed one game but was able to play the next four contests.

However, Watson suffered an aggravation of that injury last Sunday in the third quarter of a 24-9 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. He missed the remainder of the game.

The Rams signed Watson, who played his first four seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs, to a three-year, $51 million contract with $34 million guaranteed. He was part of a massive defensive overhaul that featured the Rams trading for Cleveland Browns edge-rusher Myles Garrett and Chiefs cornerback Trent McDuffie.

In seven starts, Watson amassed 24 tackles (14 solo), nine pass breakups and one interception. Opposing quarterbacks only completed 50 percent of their passes in his coverage, per Pro Football Reference . The Rams are also seventh in fewest passing yards allowed per attempt.

So this is a tough loss for the Rams, who have been shorthanded this year. Garrett has only played one game after undergoing knee surgery, but he is practicing this week. McDuffie missed two games with a groin injury and is now dealing with a back injury that kept him out of practice Wednesday.

As for Watson, he dealt with a dislocated shoulder before in 2021 when he played for Washington State, per Rams staff writer Zach Edwards .

Unfortunately, Watson will miss the rest of 2026 after suffering another dislocated shoulder plus a re-aggravation of the injury.

Hopefully he recovers well and returns to 100 percent ahead of 2027. In the meantime, Emmanuel Forbes should see more snaps.

Forbes, a former first-round pick of the Washington Commanders in 2023, is in his fourth NFL season. He's played in all eight games this year, amassing nine tackles and a pair of pass breakups.

articles.title: "We stayed together for the kids": Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce revealed the real reason she and Ed Kelce waited 25 years to divorce
articles.summary: Raising two children while managing a demanding career is never easy.
articles.body: Raising two children while managing a demanding career is never easy. For Donna Kelce, the challenge also meant putting her own happiness on hold for years. Long before her sons, Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce, became household names in the NFL, Donna and their father, Ed Kelce, faced difficulties in their marriage. In an October 2024 interview, the football stars' mother offered a rare glimpse into that chapter of her life, explaining why the couple chose to remain together despite knowing their relationship was no longer working.Donna Kelce opened up about her marriage to Ed KelceDonna and Ed Kelce spent 25 years together before eventually ending their marriage. However, their decision to stay under the same roof was not driven by the belief that everything was perfect between them. Instead, they wanted to give Travis and Jason a stable childhood.Speaking to Glamour for its Women of the Year cover story in October 2024, Donna explained how the arrangement affected her personally.“My husband and I knew that our marriage was not working, but we stayed together for the kids,” Donna explained in her Glamour Women of the Year cover story. “Ours was a very friendly relationship. So, we could do that and make sure that their life was normal as possible. But in that one respect, I did stand still for several years until I could move on on my own.”Her words offered a different perspective on the sacrifices parents sometimes make behind closed doors. Although she and Ed maintained a friendly relationship, Donna admitted that remaining in the marriage meant delaying important personal decisions.The 71-year-old also spoke about her professional life. She worked as a commercial banker across several states and carried a significant share of the family's financial responsibilities.“I was a commercial banker for a bank in several different states. I wanted to get ahead. I worked really, really hard. I was a major breadwinner in the family,” she shared. “And I think it’s important for kids to see that a woman can do whatever she wants, but I did stand still, too.”Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce's parents put their children firstDonna later discussed the decision during an appearance on The Martha Stewart Podcast in May 2024. She described raising two children as a shared responsibility and explained why she and Ed chose to delay their separation."We worked together as a team and it's very, very difficult to raise children on your own," Donna said on The Martha Stewart Podcast in May. "We decided that we would be married throughout the entire time that the kids were in the house, and that's the way it worked out."Travis also reflected on his parents' relationship in the 2023 Amazon Prime documentary Kelce. He recalled noticing certain differences at home during his middle school years, including the fact that his parents did not share a bedroom."I started making those connections when I was in middle school and realized they were probably gonna split,” he shared. “But they stayed together for me and Jason's benefit, I believe.”Looking back, Donna's comments highlighted the years of compromise behind the Kelce family's journey. articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty saw a steep drop-off in reps last week against the New York Jets, but head coach Klint Kubiak still had high praise for him on Thursday.

Kubiak said the future is still bright for the young Jeanty, adding that he's still developing.

"Ashton's a young player and has a really bright future ahead. And I'm so glad that we have him, so glad we have," Kubiak told reporters . "Him and all these young players on our roster that are continuing to grow. And it's our job as coaches to develop them."

Jeanty had just two carries in last week's win over the Raiders, while Mike Washington Jr. got the bulk of the carries, 25 for 83 yards.

Jeanty has rushed for 337 yards and a touchdown through eight games.

According to ESPN's Dan Graziano , the lack of carries was meant to be a "wake-up call" to Jeanty from the Raiders. If Jeanty continues to struggle, Las Vegas is "content to distribute the carries in Washington's favor moving forward, as he offers a more explosive element in the run game right now."

The Raiders used the No. 6 overall pick on Jeanty in 2025 and still hope he becomes a cornerstone of their franchise. Perhaps the "wake-up call" last week will help Jeanty turn things around.

articles.title: Packers' Jacobs Isn't Worrying Over Whether Additional Allegations Will Lead to More Punishment
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he isn't worrying about the possibility he may have to miss more games due to the release of allegations that were made against him years before he pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs says he isn't worrying about the possibility he may have to miss more games due to the release of allegations that were made against him years before he pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges stemming from a May altercation with his then-girlfriend.

"With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?' " Jacobs said Wednesday. " It's like, I kind of already know what it is, so it's like … it's really just up to them to make their final decision. But I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have."

After spending the first six games of the season on the commissioner's exempt list, which prevented him from playing or practicing, Jacobs has returned to play in the Packers' last two games. The NFL has said its investigation into Jacobs is ongoing, which means he still could be subject to more discipline from the league.

Jacobs pleaded no contest on Sept. 10 to charges of battery and criminal damage to property. He was arrested May 26 after his then-girlfriend said he had thrown her to the ground three days earlier.

In response to a public records request, the Hobart-Lawrence (Wisconsin) Police Department released records from their investigation Friday night that included the accounts of three other women who reported similar allegations from years before.

Lawyers representing Jacobs said he has a "substantial body of tangible evidence" disputing the allegations that surfaced in Friday's records release. They said those allegations are "old, are hearsay and easily disproven."

"It really feels like an attack on me and who I am and my character," Jacobs said Wednesday. "And at the end of the day, there's a lot of stuff being said about me that's completely false. Like, completely made up. And it's like people just run with it. And I can't change that. it's just one of those thing where it's like, 'OK, all I can do is try to be who I am and try not to let the negative moments change who I am.' And that was the biggest thing for me, throughout this whole process. I didn't want to go to a place where I felt like I was closed off and I'm angry all the time because of what's going on in my life."

Jacobs' lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III — said that one of the three women made a claim to the NFL, which reviewed it and decided no action was warranted. They said Jacobs "has kept evidence that supports his accounts and the NFL's decision."

The NFL has declined comment on the lawyers' statement. After Hobart-Lawrence police released the records that detailed the accounts from the other women, NFL spokesman Brian McCarthy had said Saturday that the league would review these allegations as part of its investigation.

Jacobs' arrest followed a May 23 incident in which police officers came to his Wisconsin home to investigate a disturbance. According to police, a woman told them Jacobs grabbed her and threw her to the ground as she was trying to exit a garage door, causing her to hit her head. Police said Jacobs also took her phone from her while she was on the ground.

Police said they noticed redness on her face and neck and could feel a bump on the back of her head.

Despite San Francisco’s depleted receiver room, the organization has no intention of bringing Aiyuk back, even after the former All-Pro claimed he is cleaning up his act. Former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Ben Roethlisberger thinks Steelers running back Jaylen Warren deserves to be in the NFL MVP conversation.

"This guy needs to start to be talked about in some MVP stuff. Like league MVP or offensive MVP. His numbers and some of the stuff he's doing is pretty impressive. His yards after contact have to be some of the highest in the league," Roethlisberger said on his Footbahlin podcast. "There's a lot of things that don't look good and then all of a sudden it's like, oh, he fell forward for three. Very rarely do you see him lose yards."

Warren has had a very impressive start to his 2026 campaign, and that continued in the team's Week 8 win over the Cleveland Browns. Overall, the Steelers rushed for 200 yards against the Browns.

It was Warren's fourth 100-yard performance of the season. Warren also has five games of 125+ yards from scrimmage this year.

Through the first eight weeks of the season, Warren has officially done something that hasn't been done in the past 10 years.

According to Kyle Borgognoni of the Fantasy Footballers , Warren's 6.9 yards per touch is the highest of any running back over the last decade through first eight games of a season.

Warren certainly has a good chance to be named first-team All-Pro this year.

And as Roethlisberger mentioned, don't count out NFL MVP or Offensive Player of the Year.

Winning NFL MVP will be awfully difficult, however. The last NFL running back to win the Associated Press NFL MVP award was Adrian Peterson, who won it for the 2012 season with the Minnesota Vikings.

articles.title: Cowboys have a chance to respond in Indianapolis
articles.summary: How optimistic are you for this week’s game?
articles.body:
The Cowboys suffered a painful 33-30 overtime loss to Arizona, but Sunday provides an immediate chance to respond.

Indianapolis is 2-6, has lost four straight games, and is coming off a 42-7 defeat against Jacksonville. The Colts also appear to be looking toward the future after trading away two of their best veteran players.

So basically Indianapolis is struggling badly and haven't won since Week 4. Their four-game losing streak includes defeats of 34-22, 26-20, 16-10 and 42-7. Sunday's 35-point loss to Jacksonville was their heaviest defeat in nearly four years and Jacksonville led the game 28-0 by halftime.

Dallas may be frustrated after Arizona, but Indianapolis enters this game with even less momentum. Daniel Jones keeps giving opponents opportunities and has thrown only five touchdowns to nine interceptions this season along with being sacked 22 times. Over his last three games alone, he has thrown five interceptions and been sacked 13 times.

Indianapolis ranks last in the NFL with a minus-11 turnover differential. Dallas is at minus-one. That is particularly encouraging after the Cowboys defense created two turnovers and five sacks against Arizona. Quinnen Williams had two sacks and has now recorded at least one in three straight games. DeMarvion Overshown also forced a fumble.

The Colts have also just traded away two stars so their roster is weaker than it was a week ago. They traded eight-time Pro Bowl guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco, both moves help Dallas.

Nelson's absence removes Indianapolis' best offensive lineman just as the Cowboys pass rush finally showed some life. Buckner's departure removes a defender who had four sacks through seven games and had been one of the Colts' most disruptive players for years. As proof how important those players were to the team, Indianapolis just played its first game without both against Jacksonville.

Indianapolis has already allowed 23 touchdowns and 2,748 yards this season. Opponents are averaging 5.7 yards per play and 4.9 yards per rushing attempt against the Colts. That gives Brian Schottenheimer options.

The way Dallas lost to Arizona was incredibly frustrating, but there were signs of improvement before the fourth-quarter collapse. The Cowboys produced five sacks and two takeaways. Shemar James recorded his first NFL interception, Overshown forced a fumble, and Williams recorded two sacks. Dallas also held Arizona to only three points in the first half and carried a 14-3 lead into halftime. The challenge is making that defensive performance last four quarters.

Against a Colts offense averaging only 19 points per game and struggling badly at quarterback, Dallas has an opportunity to do exactly that.

History provides another positive. The last Cowboys-Colts game went very well for Dallas where they won 54-19 in 2022, scoring an incredible 33 points in the fourth quarter.

Prescott threw three touchdowns, while the Dallas defense forced five turnovers, including three interceptions. It was another example of what can happen when Dallas forces Indianapolis into mistakes. That's particularly relevant this week with the Colts carrying the worst turnover differential in football.

articles.title: Court opens possibility that NFL Sunday Ticket case could expand to YouTube TV
articles.summary: On Friday, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals issued a ruling overturning a judge’s decision to toss a jury verdict levied against the NFL over antitrust vio...
articles.body:
On Friday, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals issued a ruling overturning a judge's decision to toss a jury verdict levied against the NFL over antitrust violations associated with its packaging of NFL Sunday Ticket to DirecTV. The case, which has been in the courts for about a decade, addressed whether the league violated antitrust law by compelling its Sunday Ticket provider, in this case DirecTV, to price the product artificially high so to protect the Sunday afternoon packages it sells to Fox and CBS.

A jury ruled in favor of the plaintiffs and the NFL was on the hook for $4.7 billion in damages, an amount that would be trebled to over $14 billion under federal antitrust statutes. But shortly after the jury reached its verdict, the judge overseeing the case tossed the ruling citing issues with how the plaintiffs' expert witnesses calculated the damages. On Friday, a three-judge panel ruled on the plaintiffs' subsequent appeal , deciding that the jury's assessment that the NFL was liable for the antitrust violations would stand, but the amount the league owes in damages would be retried.

But, according to a recent report by Puck's legal expert Eriq Gardner , there's another key ruling the panel of judges made that has been largely overlooked. Per Gardner, the judges filed a memorandum disposition that sent "injunction claims back to the district court to consider whether they remain viable now that the NFL's deal with DirecTV has expired."

The ongoing case deals only with a period in which the NFL licensed Sunday Ticket to DirecTV. The league's out-of-market package now, of course, is held by YouTube TV. And for all intents and purposes, NFL Sunday Ticket on YouTube TV is following the exact same model that currently has the league in hot water. Sunday Ticket remains priced at a premium rate to protect the value of CBS' and Fox's Sunday afternoon packages. Gardner suggests that sending the injunction claims back to he district court opens the possibility for those claims to be extended to YouTube TV.

"[T]here's a certain tactical logic to seeking an injunction with a newly restored liability verdict in hand. That finding wouldn't automatically establish that the YouTube TV arrangement is unlawful, but it would give the plaintiffs a substantial starting point. A credible threat to that relationship would rattle the NFL far more than another squabble over how much former DirecTV subscribers are owed," Gardner writes.

Should the plaintiffs pursue that avenue, a district court could begin considering paths that impact the NFL's Sunday Ticket package right now . Obviously, that is something the league would like to avoid at all costs.

This is partly why Gardner suggests the "most sensible ending" to this decade-long ordeal is an ending that, in hindsight, the league likely wishes it pursued a long time ago: a settlement.

It's unclear if the plaintiffs will ultimately pursue an injunction. As Gardner notes, this type of litigation is expensive and it can often take years before any investments pay off. But if the plaintiffs believe it's in their best interests to ratchet up the pressure on the NFL, this is a tactic they can use to do so. It's also the tactic that would be the most disruptive to the NFL's current business operation and how fans access games.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith Fires Back at Tom Brady’s Critics
articles.summary: Stephen A. Smith defended Tom Brady against criticism of the former quarterback’s work as a FOX NFL analyst, arguing that the scrutiny surrounding his broadc...
articles.body:
Stephen A. Smith defended Tom Brady against criticism of the former quarterback's work as a FOX NFL analyst, arguing that the scrutiny surrounding his broadcasting role has gone too far. The debate intensified after Brady challenged several officiating decisions during Green Bay's 20-17 loss to Detroit in Week 7.

Smith said Brady should be able to offer his football expertise without facing backlash. The ESPN personality's defense followed criticism over the analyst's outspoken reaction to penalties during the Packers-Lions game, particularly a late roughing-the-passer call against Green Bay defensive tackle Karl Brooks.

The disputed flag came with 2:45 remaining and extended Detroit's game-winning drive. Lions quarterback Jared Goff completed an 18-yard pass to tight end Sam LaPorta before Brooks was penalized for roughing the passer, adding 15 yards to the play. Detroit eventually scored and secured the three-point victory.

Brady questioned the ruling during the FOX broadcast, describing the contact as a bang-bang play and saying the defender had made a strong effort to bring down the quarterback. FOX rules analyst Dean Blandino agreed with the assessment, saying the tackle did not appear to involve late contact or a hit to the head or neck area. Brady also challenged other calls during the second half, including penalties involving Packers linebacker Brenton Cox Jr. and Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes.

Stephen A. Smith Blasts at NFL Icon Tom Brady's Critics

Smith fired back at those who criticized Brady after he made a mistake during a broadcast. This can be seen in a video he shared on X.

The discussion has drawn added attention because Brady is a minority owner of the Las Vegas Raiders while working as FOX's lead NFL analyst. League restrictions allow him to discuss officiating but limit criticism deemed egregious or comments questioning an official's integrity. The rules have raised questions about how candid Brady can be in the booth, though no public punishment tied to the Packers-Lions broadcast had been announced.

Smith's defense centered on Brady's experience and the role of an analyst in explaining the game. The debate over the former quarterback's commentary continues as the NFL faces scrutiny over officiating consistency, leaving the balance between broadcast candor and league rules under the spotlight. The issue could follow Brady into upcoming broadcasts, particularly as his dual role keeps his comments under close review.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Gives Honest Response to Playing at All-Pro Level for Packers in Injury Return
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers have opened three-time First Team All-Pro edge-rusher Micah Parsons' 21-day practice window as he continues his comeback from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered last December against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers have opened three-time First Team All-Pro edge-rusher Micah Parsons' 21-day practice window as he continues his comeback from a torn ACL and meniscus suffered last December against the Denver Broncos.

During a chat with reporters on Wednesday, Parsons admitted to Matt Schneidman of The Athletic that he may not be at his typical All-Pro level right away when he returns as he continues to get his conditioning and body back into playing shape.

That's understandable given that Parsons hasn't been on the field since Dec. 14, 2025. At that juncture, Parsons was enjoying an incredible 2025 season, amassing 12.5 sacks, 27 quarterback hits and 41 tackles in 14 games.

Despite missing the final three regular-season contests, Parsons earned First Team All-Pro honors and finished third in the Associated Press Defensive Player of the Year race.

Obviously, it's a great sign just to see Parsons out there.

The Packers have three weeks to activate Parsons to the roster. In theory, he could ramp up as best he can for the next few weeks and be ready for the team's Thanksgiving Eve game against the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Green Bay has a pair of games from now until then at the New England Patriots and home vs. the Minnesota Vikings.

We'll see what happens soon enough, but having Parsons out there even at less than 100 percent to start would still be a huge win for Green Bay.

He's played at an elite level for five seasons, racking up 65 sacks and 139 QB hits overall while finishing top-three in the DPOY race four times.

Getting back to that point may not happen right away, but that could certainly appear before the end of the season as the 5-3 Packers fight for the playoffs and NFC North title.

NFL legend Kurt Warner offered an encouraging assessment of Tennessee Titans quarterback Cam Ward following his performance in a narrow overtime loss to the Cincinnati Bengals. His performance marked one of his strongest outings since entering the league.

Ward completed 25 of 39 passes for 298 yards and two touchdowns, while adding 18 rushing yards. He connected with multiple receivers and helped Tennessee remain within striking distance as the game moved into overtime. He also showed improved decision-making, limiting mistakes while handling pressure from Cincinnati's defensive front.

The Titans' offense found success through a balanced approach, with Tony Pollard contributing on the ground and the passing game producing several key plays. Ward's ability to sustain drives gave Tennessee a chance to secure its first win in a difficult matchup. However, the Bengals ultimately prevailed after converting a late opportunity in the extra period.

The performance offered a potential turning point for a Tennessee team that has struggled to establish consistency. Ward has faced pressure to deliver results as the franchise evaluates its roster and long-term direction, but his showing against Cincinnati provided a more encouraging outlook. The quarterback's growth remains central to the Titans' rebuilding effort.

Warner's assessment adds to the growing attention surrounding Ward's development, particularly as Tennessee approaches the NFL trade deadline.
